The bug was `first = next(cond[1].flatten())` — `cond` is the list of tokens for the first WHEN condition (e.g. `foo = 1`), so indexing with `[1]` either raised `IndexError: list index out of range` (when the condition had zero or one tokens) or grabbed the wrong token for offset calculation. Changed it to `cond[0]`, which is the correct first token of the condition to align indentation against.

Verified manually:
- `CASE WHEN foo = 1 THEN 2 WHEN foo = 3 THEN 4 ELSE 5 END` reindents correctly with proper alignment (fixes 'format reindent: case').
- `CASE 1 WHEN 1 THEN 2 WHEN 3 THEN 4 ELSE 5 END` (case with an operand) reindents correctly without raising IndexError (fixes 'format reindent: case2').
- `compact=True` with a CASE expression collapses onto one line without error (fixes 'compact').

This is a minimal, targeted one-character-index fix that restores prior correct behavior without affecting other reindent logic.
